entry.title: Why I Bet My Engineering Career on .NET 9 (And Left Legacy PHP Behind)
entry.summary: When I started my journey in software engineering, I spent a lot of time in the trenches of legacy web development. I maintained spaghetti PHP codebases, patched SQL injection vulnerabilities in systems used by thousands of students, and wrestled with the chaos of loosely typed languages. It was a necessary education. But it wasn’t the future. Today, as a Software Engineer based in Verona, I have pivoted entirely to the Microsoft Stack (.NET 9). Here is why I believe C# and Blazor are the only viable choice for building secure, scalable enterprise systems in 2025. In my early days of building automation scripts and web tools, “undefined is not a function” was a daily nightmare. In the enterprise world—where I now focus on CRM architecture—you cannot afford runtime errors. C# gives me the strictness I need. If the code compiles, it (mostly) works. The transition from legacy PHP to strongly typed C# changed the way I think about data. I don’t just move JSON around; I define Models, Contracts, and Interfaces. This makes the software predictable and secure by design. For years, “Full Stack” meant context-switching between a backend language (Python/Java) and a frontend framework (React/Angular). With Blazor WebAssembly, I write C# on the server and C# in the browser. I come from a background of low-level automation and WinAPI optimization. I care about milliseconds. There is a reason enterprise companies in Northern Italy (and the world) run on .NET. It is stable, it is fast, and it is mature. .NET Specialist. I don’t chase the JavaScript framework of the week. I build systems that last. I am Mehdi Ouassou, a Software Engineer and .NET Developer. You can view my portfolio and projects at mehdiouassou.it.
